No, not directly. The JRC map (GFC2020 V4) is a snapshot of forest cover in 2020, so it can't show a 2023 loss. The loss itself comes from the Hansen/UMD series, which records 0.7 ha of tree-cover loss in 2023 (1.2% of the 58.1 ha asset).

What JRC does show is that 100% of the loss area was mapped as forest in 2020. That means the loss happened on land that was forest at the baseline. Together with Hansen observations for later years, through 2025, this meets the run's corroboration rule.
